exposure: Parity 5-10 (analyzed separately for each parity level)
cohort: The study involved grand multiparous women (parity 5-10) with singleton gestation who delivered in one of four university-affiliated obstetrical centers in a single geographic area between 2003 and 2021.
finding: Grand multiparity (parity 8-10) was associated with a significantly increased risk of PPH, placental abruption, LGA neonates, neonatal hypoglycemia, and neonatal seizures, but a reduced likelihood of unplanned cesarean deliveries, preterm deliveries, vacuum-assisted deliveries, SGA neonates, and severe perineal tears.
